changed_requirement_text.after: Malformed-message handling MUST follow the HTTP version in use before application status mapping. For HTTP/1.1, a request with invalid Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding framing, or with both fields, MUST be rejected with 400 and connection closure (RFC 9112, Sections 6.1 and 6.3). An otherwise well-framed request without the Content-Length required by DHB1-001 MUST receive 411, including an otherwise valid chunked HTTP/1.1 request (RFC 9110, Section 15.5.12; RFC 9112, Section 6.3). HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 stream and connection error requirements (RFC 9113, Section 8.1.1; RFC 9114, Section 4.1.2) take precedence over this status mapping; an HTTP error response alone does not satisfy a required stream reset. For requests that pass framing checks, status mapping MUST be 401 for unauthenticated requests, 400 for invalid requests within the byte cap, 413 for an exceeded byte cap, 503 with body {"error": "retry"} for a retryable condition with nothing issued, and 500 for an internal failure. The only success status for the decision exchange MUST be 200.
